title: Adverse outcome pathway-based analysis of liver steatosis in vitro using human liver cell lines
protocol: Thaw one cryovial and seed it in a 25 cm² flask.
Incubate the cells for 14 days before splitting them into three 75 cm² flasks.
Grow the cells in the 75 cm² flasks for another 14 days until they are ready to be split again or seeded directly into plates depending on the desired assay format (6- or 96-well plates).
Split the cells once more if grown in 75 cm² flasks, otherwise allow them to continue growing in differentiation medium for another 14 days.
Seed HepaRG cells into 96-well or 6-well plates and incubate with differentiation medium for an additional 14 days until fully differentiated.
Administer treatment medium (TM) on day 28 for gene expression analysis or on day 30 for WST-1 and TGA assays.
Incubate cells with test substance at day 30 for 24 hours or at day 32 for 72 hours as required by the specific assay.
Pre-warm the proliferation medium in a water bath to 37°C.
Transfer 7 mL of pre-warmed proliferation medium to a 25 cm² bottle.
Thaw the frozen HepaRG cryovial quickly (1–2 min) in a water bath while swirling until only a small ice crystal remains.
Quickly transfer the thawed HepaRG cells into the prepared cell culture flask and distribute it equally by swirling in a back-and-forth and side-to-side manner.
Change medium 5–6 h after thawing using 7 mL of pre-warmed proliferation medium.
Change medium every 2–3 days using 7 mL proliferation medium (Mon.-Wed.-Fri.).
After 14 days, split the initial 25 cm² flask (passage 0) into three 75 cm² flasks (passage 1) without counting the cells.
Wash cells with approx. 5 mL sterile PBS.
Add 1 mL of trypsin-EDTA (0.05%) in Dulbecco’s phosphate-buffered saline to the cells and distribute it on the cells by swirling.
Trypsinize cells for approximately 5 minutes at 37°C.
Neutralize the trypsin by adding 5 mL of proliferation medium.
Separate cells using a serological pipette by pipetting up and down and pressing against the bottom of the flask.
Mix cells thoroughly by pulling them through a 1 mL combitip if necessary.
Add 12 mL of pre-warmed proliferation medium to each of three 75 cm² flasks.
Add 2 mL HepaRG cell suspension to each flask, mix well.
Distribute the mixture gently by swirling back-and-forth and side-to-side in each flask.
Change the medium every 2–3 days using proliferation medium.
After 14 days, split cells from 75 cm² flasks into new 75 cm² flasks for further propagation.
Seed cells from 75 cm² flasks into 96-well plates for cytotoxicity testing or TGA assay.
Seed cells from 75 cm² flasks into 6-well plates for gene expression analysis.
Wash the cells with approximately 10 mL sterile PBS.
Add 2 mL of trypsin-EDTA (0.05%) in Dulbecco’s phosphate-buffered saline and distribute by swirling.
Trypsinize cells for approximately 5 min at 37°C.
Neutralize the trypsin by adding 12 mL proliferation medium.
Separate cells by pipetting up and down using a serological pipette and pressing against the bottom of the flask.
Count the cells using trypan blue exclusion; the percentage of dead cells should not exceed 10%.
Seed the cells in the desired plate/flask format as specified.
Calculate the volume of cell suspension required for 2 million cells and fill up to 14 mL with proliferation medium as required.
Prepare a cell suspension of 7 mL with 90,000 cells/mL in pre-warmed proliferation medium for one 96-well plate.
Mix the cell suspension by swirling back-and-forth and side-to-side manner without vortexing.
Distribute the cell suspension to inner 60 wells using 100 μL/well.
Fill outer wells with 200 μL PBS to avoid evaporation.
Prepare a 100,000 cells/mL suspension in pre-warmed proliferation medium for 6-well plate.
Distribute 2 mL of the cell suspension in each well of the 6-well plate using serological pipette.
Grow cells in incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 without moving for next 5–6 hours to allow attachment.
Change medium every 2–3 days using proliferation medium.
Carefully aspirate the medium from cells seeded in 96-well or 6-well plates on day 14 post-seeding.
Add pre-warmed transition medium containing 1% DMSO using 2 mL/6-well plate (for gene expression analysis) and 100 μL/96-well plate for WST-1 and TGA assay.
Replace the transition medium with differentiation medium containing 1.7% DMSO on day 16.
Change the medium every 2–3 days using differentiation medium until day 28 (for 6-well plates) or day 30 (for 96-well plates).
Aspirate the medium from 6-well plates at day 28 and replace with pre-warmed treatment medium.
Aspirate the medium of the 96-well plates carefully.
Replace with pre-warmed treatment medium.
Incubate HepaRG cells with test substances for 30 minutes.
Determine the highest non-toxic concentration using a cytotoxicity assay such as WST-1.
Ensure cell viability is greater than 90%.
Perform gene expression analysis using the highest non-toxic concentration.
For reporter gene and TGA assays, prepare a 1:2 serial dilution of the highest non-toxic concentration in addition to the full concentration.
Include a solvent control as a negative control for all test compounds.
Use dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) as the solvent for all test compounds, which is also present in HepaRG-differentiation medium.
Adapt DMSO concentrations based on cell type: 0.1% for HepG2 and 0.5% for HepaRG cells.
If another solvent is used, adjust concentrations accordingly and include an additional solvent control.
Pre-warm TM and TM without DMSO.
Thaw the stock solution of the test substance at room temperature.
Thaw the stock solutions of the positive controls at room temperature.
Prepare a 1.2 ml/plate solution as concentration 8 (C8) using TM without DMSO for the WST-1 assay.
Prepare 2.2 mL/well of the test concentration by diluting the stock solution in TM without DMSO for gene expression analysis.
Prepare a 2.4 mL/plate as concentration 8 (C8) using TM without DMSO for TGA assay.
Add 0.5 ml of C8 to 0.5 ml TM for C7.
Add 0.5 ml of C7 to 0.5 ml TM for C6.
Continue serial dilution until reaching C1.
Incubate the diluted solutions in an incubator.
Prepare 1 mL/96-well plate of 10% Triton X-100 stock solution diluted 1:1000 in TM for WST-1 assay.
Prepare 6.8 mL/6-well plate of 8 mM Imazalil stock solution diluted 1:200 in TM without DMSO for gene expression analysis.
Prepare 1 mL/96-well plate of 2 mM T0901317 stock solution diluted 1:200 in TM without DMSO for TGA assay.
Aspirate the medium carefully from the wells.
Replace the aspirated medium with solvent control, test substance dilutions, and positive controls using 100 μL/96-well and 2 mL/6-well.
Ensure complete aspiration of the whole volume in each well to achieve correct concentration of test substances.
Avoid touching the cell monolayer during aspiration.
Do not use a combitip for adding test substances and controls; adjust speed appropriately to avoid damaging the cell monolayer or causing droplets to stick.
Maintain minimal time between aspiration and addition of test substances and controls to prevent drying of cells.
Incubate HepG2 cells with the test substances and controls for 24 hours.
Incubate HepaRG cells with the test substances and controls for 72 hours.
Thaw one WST-1 aliquot (1 mL) per plate at 37°C for approximately 2 minutes and vortex thoroughly.
Inspect each blank well on the plate using an inverted microscope to check for visible precipitate formed by the test substance.
Note the concentration of the test substance if it forms a visible precipitate.
Add 10 μL of WST-1 solution per well (including blanks).
Incubate HepG2 cells for 23 hours.
Incubate HepaRG cells for 71 hours.
Incubate cells with WST-1 tetrazolium salt for 60 minutes in a cell culture incubator.
Determine the plate reader settings for measurement.
Insert the plate into the plate reader after 60-minute incubation and start measurement.
Save raw data upon completion of the measurement.
Discard the plate after measurement.
Create an Excel file for data analysis.
Copy raw data to the first sheet in the Excel file.
Use the second sheet in the Excel file for further analysis.
Subtract the blank from each value of the respective concentration/control.
Calculate mean and standard deviation of the three technical replicates.
Determine cell viability by relating measurements to the solvent control and multiplying by 100.
Average control/concentration group values to obtain cell viability in percent normalized to the solvent control.
Repeat steps using different cell passages to obtain three independent biological replicates.
Calculate the highest non-toxic concentration where cell viability is greater than 90%.
Seed HepG2 cells as described in materials and equipment and cultivate for 24 h in a cell culture incubator.
After 23 h, use an inverted microscope to control cells regarding cell morphology, viability, and confluency (optimal confluency: 30%–40%, minimum: 25%).
Let the transfection reagent TransIT-LT1, Opti-MEM, and plasmids thaw until they reach room temperature.
Determine the required amount of plasmid DNA per well based on the nuclear receptor being used.
Use 40 ng/well for both NR and firefly luciferase plasmid in TAA assays.
Use 80 ng/well of p3xDREC (AHR) plasmid for RGA with AHR assays.
Include 1 ng/well of renilla plasmid for all assays.
Ensure plasmids are of transfection grade purity and their concentration is determined beforehand.
Vortex the TransIT-LT1 before use.
Gently vortex the plasmid DNA stocks before use.
Prepare the transfection medium by adding plasmid DNA to Opti-MEM and mix carefully by pipetting up and down.
Add TransIT-LT1 to the mixture and mix carefully by pipetting up and down.
Incubate for 20–30 minutes at room temperature.
Mix again carefully by pipetting up and down after incubation.
Slowly add 10 μL of the transfection master mix to each well and rock the plate to distribute evenly.
Observe cells using an inverted microscope regarding cell morphology, viability, and confluency after 4 hours.
Aspirate the transfection medium after 4-6 hours post-transfection.
Add 100 μL/well of negative or positive control and test substances.
Incubate for 24 h in the cell culture incubator.
Use an inverted microscope to check cells for morphology, viability, and confluency after 24 h.
Aspirate the medium carefully.
Add 50 μl lysis buffer per well using a multi-channel pipette.
Shake the 96-well plate for 15 min at RT on the microtiter plate shaker at 600 rpm.
Centrifuge the 96-well plate for 5 minutes at 3,000 × g.
Store the plate at -80°C or continue with the luminescence measurement.
Prepare Fluc injection solution 30 minutes before starting the measurement.
Prepare Rluc injection solution 30 minutes before starting the measurement.
Thaw frozen plates for approximately 20 minutes at room temperature.
Switch on the microplate reader with injectors at least 30 minutes before measurement.
Transfer 5 μL of lysate from each well to a white microtiter plate.
Leave the first row empty for assessing background signal.
Work in dim light conditions to avoid influencing the background signal.
Store plates in the dark for at least 10 minutes before use.
Insert inceptor needles in the Fluc injector solution protected from light.
Insert inceptor needles in the Rluc injector solution protected from light.
Use the setup of the software to completely fill the tubes with Fluc and Rluc using 2 mL each.
Insert the injector into the machine and insert the plate.
Determine the wells to be measured, including the first empty row.
Start the measurement.
Do not continue measurement if the empty wells have a background signal > 20.
Save the raw data when all measurements are completed.
Empty the tubes after completing measurements.
Perform cleaning steps according to the instructions of the microplate reader used.
Divide all firefly signals by renilla signals for data analysis.
Analyze receptor activation for all receptors except PPARα.
Normalize the data by dividing the firefly by the renilla values, followed by division with the mean of the solvent control.
Determine the mean and standard deviation from the three technical replicates for each condition.
Repeat steps using different cell passages to obtain three independent biological replicates.
Calculate the mean and standard deviation for the repeated steps.
Perform the non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test followed by Dunn’s test using a statistical software like SigmaPlot 14.
Test further for significant activation of PPARα with p < 0.05 and induction > 1.5 relative to solvent control.
Assume receptor antagonism if p < 0.05 and concentration-dependent repression < 0.7 relative to the solvent control.
Repeat steps by coincubating 25 nm GW7647 with test substances.
Analyze receptor activation in comparison to 25 nM GW7647 for further testing.
Perform the non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test.
Conduct Dunn’s test following the Kruskal-Wallis test.
Assume receptor antagonism with p < 0.05 and repression < 0.7 relative to 25 nM GW7647.
Repeat step 15–19.e for PPARα if receptor antagonism of PPARα is observed.
Include 25 nM GW7647 as an additional condition in the repeat test.
Co-incubate test substance dilutions with 25 nM GW7647 during repeated testing.
Analyze receptor activation in relation to GW7647 alone.
Incubate cells with the highest non-toxic concentration of test compounds for 24 hours.
Include a solvent control and a positive control (40 μM Imazalil) in the incubation.
Start initial experiments with two 6-well plates corresponding to ten different test compounds.
Observe cells regarding cell morphology, viability, and confluency after 24 h incubation.
Chill PBS on ice to 4°C.
Take the incubated plate from the cell culture incubator and put it on ice.
Aspirate the wells with treatment medium of test substances and controls carefully.
Wash each well gently twice with 2 mL of ice-cold PBS using a serological pipette.
Add 350 μL cell lysis buffer per well using a pipette and a filter tip.
Scrape off the cells by pipetting up and down.
Transfer the lysates into 2 mL reaction tubes.
Place the tubes on ice.
Store cell lysates at −80°C until further processing if not used immediately.
Thaw samples on ice before use, avoiding freeze/refreeze cycles.
Isolate total RNA using the RNeasy Mini Kit following Qiagen’s protocol.
Integrate DNase digestion using the RNase-Free DNase Set and protocol to exclude DNA contamination.
Elute RNA from the RNeasy spin column membrane by adding 50 μL RNase-free water directly to the membrane.
Close the lid gently and centrifuge for 1 min at ≥ 8000 × g (≥ 10,000 rpm).
Assess quality and quantity of isolated RNA using an appropriate quantification tool such as the NanoDrop spectrophotometer by measuring absorbance at 260 nm and 280 nm.
Thaw RNA samples and the High-Capacity cDNA Reverse Transcription Kit on ice.
Prepare the 2× RT master mix according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Place the 2× RT master mix on ice and mix gently without vortexing.
Calculate the required volume for 1 μg total RNA for each sample.
Add the appropriate volume of each RNA sample (containing 1 μg total RNA) to a PCR clean reaction tube using a pipette.
Add nuclease-free water to result in a total volume of 5 μL.
Add 5 μL of the 2× RT master mix to each reaction tube containing RNA.
Mix gently by pipetting up and down.
Close the reaction tubes and briefly centrifuge them to spin down the contents and eliminate any air bubbles.
Place the reaction tubes on ice until they are ready to be loaded into the thermocycler.
Program the thermocycler according to the settings provided.
Load the reaction tubes into the thermocycler and start the run.
Briefly centrifuge the reaction tubes after the run to spin down evaporated water.
Dilute cDNA samples 1:5 by adding 40 μL nuclease-free water.
Thaw cDNA samples, primer working solutions, and the Maxima SYBR Green/ROX qPCR Master Mix on ice.
Prepare a primer-SYBR-green master mix (PCR Master Mix) for each primer pair following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Vortex primers before use to allow homogeneous distribution of the oligonucleotides.
Work with dimmed lights when handling SYBR-green to avoid loss of fluorescent signal intensity.
Gently mix reaction tubes and briefly centrifuge them to spin down contents and eliminate air bubbles.
Place PCR master mixes on ice in the dark until use.
Pipette 9 μL of respective PCR master mix into the PCR 384 well plate using an electronic pipet with a combitip or manual pipet.
Add 1 μL of respective cDNA sample to each well for amplification of reference genes and genes of interest.
Provide 1 μL of nuclease-free water to each well of no template control (NTC) for amplification control of each primer pair-specific mastermix.
Cover the plate tightly with a self-adhesive PCR film.
Centrifuge the plate for 1 min at 1000 × g.
Check single, specific PCR products by melting curve analysis.
Assign a common threshold for reference genes and genes of interest.
Adjust baseline for each primer pair separately.
Adjust baseline for each primer pair.
Include enough cycles to eliminate background signals.
Determine Ct values of all target and housekeeping genes for each sample.
Calculate relative gene expression levels related to untreated control using the 2-ΔΔCt method.
Normalize to the geometric mean of both housekeeping genes.
Repeat steps using different cell passages to obtain three independent biological replicates.
Calculate the mean and standard deviation.
Express gene expression results obtained from 2-ΔΔCt calculation as log2 fold changes.
Multiply log2 values for each marker gene with LASSO regression coefficients.
Sum all 10 classificatory values to obtain compound-specific “log ratio with lambda coefficient”.
Perform steps 1–11 to obtain differentiated 96-well plates of HepaRG cells incubated with the test substances and controls for the TGA assay for 72 h.
Approximately 15 minutes before the end of incubation, use an inverted microscope to inspect the cells regarding their density, morphology, and viability.
Prepare 18 mL of a 5 μg/mL Hoechst 33342 in PBS for use in a 96-well plate.
Aspirate the medium after 72 h incubation and wash each well with 200 μL PBS.
Add 200 μL of the Hoechst solution to each well.
Add 5 μL AdipoRed row-wise to each well, briefly rocking the plate after each addition.
Shake the plate for 1 min at 600 rpm on a microtiter plate shaker.
Incubate the plate for 10 min at 37°C in the cell culture incubator.
Determine the appropriate settings for the plate reader for measurement.
Insert the plate into the plate reader and start the measurement.
Save the raw data when the measurement is complete.
Create an Excel sheet for data analysis.
Copy raw data to the first sheet of the Excel document.
Use the second sheet for further data analysis.
Normalize AdipoRed signals by dividing them by Hoechst signals.
Determine relative induction to the solvent control by dividing each value by the mean of the solvent control values.
Calculate the mean and standard deviation of technical replicates.
Accept results when the positive control shows an induction of triglycerides > 2.
Omit a maximum of one outlier among six technical replicates if the coefficient of variation is >30%.
Repeat steps using different cell passages to obtain three independent biological replicates.
Calculate the mean and standard deviation for the obtained data.
Perform a Shapiro-Wilk-Test on the mean relative induction of all conditions and controls using statistical software such as SigmaPlot 14.
Determine if results are normally distributed based on the Shapiro-Wilk-Test.
Continue with one-way ANOVA followed by Dunnett’s test for multiple comparisons against the solvent control if results are normally distributed.
Continue with the non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test.
Follow up with Dunn’s test for multiple comparisons.
Classify the test substance as steatosis-positive when the relative induction is > 1.5 and p < 0.05 in at least one concentration.
Classify the test substance as steatosis-negative when the relative induction is < 1.5 in all tested concentrations.
Increase the incubation time up to seven days or refresh the treatment medium every 2–3 d if necessary.
Consider that a test substance might be metabolized too slowly/too quickly in cell culture settings.
Analyze mixture effects for 3 hours.
Perform step 30 for 2 hours.
Complete step 31 within 1 hour.
Select “use example date sets” and choose “example dataset of continuous response” in the drop-down menu.
Select dose-response analysis, name the analysis, and click on “Next: Specify”.
Select all single test substances ("A" and "B") as “Dose column(s)”.
Select “Compound” as “Single doses and mixture column”.
Select the column with the response (“mean”) as “Response column(s)”.
Select “Continuous, summary data” as type of response data.
Choose the column for the dispersion measure (standard deviation or standard error of the mean).
Choose the group size (“N”).
Set “BMR (CES)” to 0.5 and leave the preset AIC criterion at 2 (default).
Click on “Run”.
Mix compound A and B in a 1:1 ratio.
For example, mix 500 μM compound A (RPF of 1) with 250 μM compound B (RPF of 2).
Perform TGA, qPCR, and RGA using the single substances and the designed equipotent mixture.
Perform three independent experiments.
Analyze the mixture effect by modelling the data using PROAST.
Add single substances again for each mixture test.
Model concentration-response using a four-parameter model in PROAST.
Prepare data of TGA as continuous, summary data using Excel.
Include the concentration of the single substances in columns A and B.
